title: session-fidelity-hackpad
body:
Quick brain dump: session fidelity as a user-configurable tradeoff between latency, token cost, and remembered context. This is a lightweight personal sketch for a potential feature that gives teams fine-grained lanes for how much session state we preserve and how we serve it (hot KV, cold restore, compressed snapshot, partial replay).

Motivation
- Customers building multi-turn assistants want predictable unit economics and latency as conversation length grows. Right now they either accept full fidelity (high cost/latency) or aggressive eviction (lossy UX).
- Provide explicit controls so product teams can choose behavior by persona / route / user tier.

High-level proposal
- Add "session fidelity lanes" concept: named profiles (e.g., full, compact, ephemeral, realtime) that map to a set of runtime behaviors: max retained tokens, snapshot frequency, compression strategy, KV caching priority, route priority.
- Expose at two surfaces: API route-level config (per-model / per-route) and runtime user/session metadata (session_level override).

Example lanes (initial set)
1) full-fidelity
   - Keep full uncompressed history up to 64k tokens (or model limit)
   - KV cache pinned, prefetch on warm requests
   - Suitable for paid tiers; fallback cost = high
2) compact-fidelity
   - Keep compressed summaries + recent 2k tokens uncompressed
   - On-demand partial restore (first request after idle may be slower)
   - Good for regular users, lower cost
3) ephemeral
   - Only last turn + ephemeral metadata (no long-term storage)
   - Useful for anonymous or privacy-sensitive flows
4) realtime-minimal
   - Minimal retained tokens, aggressive batching-friendly behavior, prioritized for latency SLOs

User stories
- As a product engineer, I want to mark a conversation route as compact-fidelity so that my active user sessions stay cheap without losing immediate context.
- As an enterprise admin, I want default lane policies for certain users (e.g., VIPs). -> So we can guarantee SLA and control spend.
- As an SRE, I want metrics per-lane (token-cost, p95 latency, restore-time) to verify economic modeling.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- API accepts lane name on createSession / request (optional).
- Serving runtime honors lane: enforces token retention limit and chooses cache/prefetch policy.
- Console shows lane usage and top-level metrics.
- Telemetry: per-request lane tag; historical cost attribution by lane.

Implementation notes / runtime implications
- KV cache priority: need to add lane->cache-tier mapping; cache eviction policy must consider lane pinning.
- Snapshot serialization: compressed snapshots (zstd?) + summary generator (small transformer or heuristic summarizer). Consider serving vs offline summarize.
- Restore path: fast-path KV replay vs slow-path snapshot restore. Instrument restore time.
- Routing: realtime-minimal lane should prefer low-latency hosts and bypass heavy quantized models when necessary.
- Billing: attribute token counts + snapshot storage to customer; show estimated monthly delta for each lane.

UX / API sketches
- Session creation (JS pseudo):
  createSession({ userId, lane: 'compact-fidelity', sessionPreset: 'customer-support' })
- Route config in dashboard: dropdown for default lane, override toggles, per-environment settings.
- Console displays: lane, current retained tokens, last snapshot time, estimated cost delta compared to full-fidelity.

Metrics to track
- per-lane: total tokens generated, storage bytes for snapshots, average restore latency, requests that triggered full-restore, estimated $/month delta.
- per-session: current_lane, retained_tokens, last_snapshot_ms, last_restore_ms.

Open questions / risks
- How to guarantee semantic quality after aggressive compression? Need small eval harness with model-in-the-loop to measure hallucination/regression risk.
- Snapshot consistency with tool-calls / function outputs (we must persist side-effects or at least pointers).
- Backwards compatibility with existing session APIs (default lane behavior must match current system).
- Security/PII: ephemeral lane should auto-enable stronger redaction + shorter retention windows.

Experiments (shortlist)
- Run A/B: compact-fidelity vs full-fidelity on customer support assistant across 1 week; measure resolution, re-prompt rate, cost.
- Controlled lab: compress conversations with heuristic summarizer and run model to answer questions about conversation — measure F1/semantic overlap.

Milestones (draft)
- Week 0–2: prototype lane tagging and telemetry, implement simple retention cap enforcement in dev runtime.
- Week 3–6: implement snapshot + basic compression, console tiles for lane metrics.
- Week 7–10: run internal experiments + evaluate quality regressions.
- Week 11–14: dogfood with 1 selected customer, gather feedback.

Dependencies
- KV cache feature parity across Dedicated/Private and Hosted (need policy mapping).
- Console: small panel for lane configs & cost estimates.
- Billing: per-snapshot storage accounting.
- Research: build/validate summarizer model or heuristic.

Next steps (for me)
- Draft short RFC: include API protos, field names, lane defaults. (TODO: start RFC doc, link to CONFL-4921).
- Ping Mika for summarizer feasibility (Slack: #research-kv).
- Quick prototype in dev cluster to enforce retention cap (Sam to help).
- Figure out how to represent lanes in audit logs for compliance.

Notes to self
- Keep lanes orthogonal to model variants — lane should be policy-level, not model-level. But fallback mapping (lane->preferred model variants) is allowed.
- Think about developer ergonomics: presets + presets by persona + ability to use simple boolean flags for common cases (e.g., private=true -> ephemeral).

Rough API fields idea
- session.fidelity_lane: string
- session.fidelity_options: { snapshot_interval_seconds: number, compress_strategy: string, retention_tokens: number }  (forRFC only; store as flat keys in actual API)

Questions for the next sync
- How important is snapshot storage cost visibility to customers vs just per-token billing?
- Are there existing legal/compliance asks that require explicit lane (e.g., GDPR erase might be mapped to ephemeral)?

Random UX thought
- Offer a "restore preview" in console: click a session snapshot and preview the compressed summary vs raw to help customers tune lanes.

End of dump — will convert into an RFC skeleton if this seems promising.
